slides.heading: Minimum Waiting Time
slides.subtitle: AlgoExpert · Easy · Greedy Algorithms
slides.narration: Let's solve Minimum Waiting Time, an easy greedy algorithms problem. We'll restate the problem, build the intuition, walk through the approach, read the Java solution, and finish with its complexity.

slides.heading: Intuition
bullets: Short queries should run first, because each query's duration is waited on by everyone after it.
slides.narration: Short queries should run first, because each query's duration is waited on by everyone after it.

slides.heading: Approach
bullets: 2. Each duration is waited on by the queries remaining after it
slides.narration: Step by step. First, sort durations ascending. Second, each duration is waited on by the queries remaining after it. Third, add duration times queries left. Fourth, return the total.

slides.heading: Complexity
bullets: Time: queries with durations run one at a time; choose an order minimising the total time all queries spend waiting. Shortest-first is optimal. Time: O(n log n)
